items.title: Schwab Enters Altcoin Market
points: Major retail brokerage Charles Schwab added altcoin trading (buying/selling cryptocurrencies other than Bitcoin and Ethereum) to its platform for the first time.
The move signals institutional confidence in altcoins and reflects growing retail demand for diversified crypto exposure.
Schwab's entry typically triggers broader industry adoption, as competitors follow established players into new asset classes.
Regulatory clarity around altcoins may improve as major brokerages build formal trading infrastructure and compliance frameworks.

items.title: MicroStrategy Bitcoin Holdings Turn Unrealized Loss
points: 849,327 BTC now valued at $63.58B against a $64.08B acquisition cost, breaking Michael Saylor's psychological floor.
Average purchase price of $75,451 per coin represents the company's de facto breakeven threshold after months of leveraged buying.
Move puts pressure on Saylor's thesis that continuous accumulation at any price would prove profitable long-term.

items.title: Walraswap: Decentralized Exchange Innovation Solving Solver Manipulation
points: Equilibrium-based batch decentralized exchange (DEX, a platform for trading crypto without a central intermediary) integrates external automated market maker (AMM, a system that prices trades using a formula and liquidity pools) liquidity, finding price vectors where all orders execute with zero token surplus or deficit.
Solvers (entities that match buy and sell orders) can no longer censor orders to shift prices in their favor—their only remaining attack surface is detectable in repeated game play.

Unlike CoW Swap, UniswapX, and 1inch Fusion which use uniform clearing prices, Walraswap frames settlement as a convex optimization problem (a mathematical technique guaranteeing fairness), making net trades unique.

items.title: Onchain Credit Market Captures GPU Financing Gap
points: $197B in public GPU (graphics processing unit, hardware used for AI computing) financings since 2023 funded mostly by big banks serving only large borrowers; USD.AI targets the underserved small neocloud segment.

USD.AI charges 10-15% rates (12% median) versus 9-10% bank rates, offers 7-day loan clearance, has originated $531M across 20 deals, and runs a 7% yield vault with a loan-resale program (GLX) to recycle capital.
First GLX exit: $98.1M Duos Edge AI loan repaid in 4 months; onchain lenders still hold under 1% of the $48.4B total GPU debt market, leaving room for growth.

items.title: Crypto Cards: Reality Check on Headline Cashback Rates
points: Only 256 of 646 tracked crypto debit/credit cards are actually live; analyst Kseilas ranked 109 based on cost (30%), cashback (25%), safety (20%), access (15%), daily use (10%).
Top S-tier picks: ether.fi Cash (3% on first $2K/month in ETHFI token), Solid (up to 3% in USDC, capped $50/month), Ethena Pay (4% in AVAX on first $2.5K), Jupiter (2% in USDC).
Catch: most headline rates require own-token payouts, staking (locking crypto to earn rewards), or minimum balances; OKX wins for travel (no EU FX fee), Coinbase One best for Bitcoin credit.

items.title: Base Denim Upgrade Shrinks Stale Price Windows for Traders
points: Proprietary automated market maker (propAMM) operators face execution risk: a 1-block gap between onchain quoted price and live market rate lets fast traders extract value from makers.
Base's Denim converts each 200ms flashblock (fast execution block) into a full block, shrinking price staleness from 2 seconds to 200ms and giving solvers fresher quotes sooner.

Execution advantage shifts from tip size (paying more for priority) to sequencer latency (physical proximity to block production), a dynamic Biconomy has tested with a major market maker since October.
